_description: Mailchimp marketing-email audit-log + activity export → AKSI control ID mapping. Mailchimp is the dominant marketing-email platform — agents that orchestrate marketing campaigns, manage audiences, schedule automations, or push list updates surface here. Where SendGrid governs transactional + marketing send, Mailchimp is marketing-first: every campaign has CAN-SPAM exposure (US — required physical-postal-address line, working unsubscribe link, recorded consent for the recipient), GDPR exposure for any EU subscriber (consent must be explicit opt-in, not legitimate-interest), sender-reputation exposure (deliverability_score, complaint_rate, bounce_rate, SPF/DKIM/DMARC/BIMI authentication), and audience-PII exposure (importing/exporting/deleting member lists with PII columns). Audit-log event_type drives primary signal selection; campaign / audience / action_metadata payloads add additive control findings. Marketing campaigns sent without recorded consent_basis (consent_basis=null) are surfaced as DE-01 FAIL — direct CAN-SPAM violation indicator parallel to SendGrid. Marketing to EU subscribers under anything other than explicit opt-in is PR-04 FAIL (GDPR consent missing for EU). Missing unsubscribe link or missing physical-address line is PR-05 FAIL — CAN-SPAM hard-required mechanics. Mailchimp's pre-send compliance check failing is PR-04 FAIL. Sender-domain authentication missing (any of SPF / DKIM / DMARC false) is PR-04 FAIL — bad reputation guarantee on a marketing send. Cross-list pattern (one actor touching > N audience_ids in 1h) and high-volume marketing (one actor > N campaigns / > X recipients in 24h) generate synthetic PR-04 FLAGs. Email addresses are NEVER stored in full — only the @domain portion of actor.email survives. Campaign subject text is dropped (length only); audience.id and campaign.audience_id are reduced to the last 8 characters; audience.name is dropped (length only); webhook URLs are reduced to host only; action_metadata.ip_address is masked to /16.
